properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 15 at 12:03PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Through Friday morning, a series of fronts will bring multiple
rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall across the Alaska Panhandle.
The first ongoing front is expected to bring 1 to 1.5 inches of rain
to the northern half of the panhandle today. The second round of
heavy rain is expected to bring an additional 0.5 to 1.5 inches
tonight into Friday morning, with the higher end QPF amounts
expected for Baranof and Admiralty Islands. More localized lower or
higher amounts are possible due to terrain effects. A brief lull in
the heavier precipitation amounts is expected during the afternoon
hours today.

Even higher rain amounts are possible for parts of the central
panhandle associated with the front tonight as its low develops
inland and moves northward, though there is still a lack of
confidence on the exact location of these higher rates. As of now,
the highest amounts are expected to move into southern Baranof
Island up into Stephens Passage, though some elevated rainfall
amounts may still reach Sitka and other parts of the central and
northern panhandle.

While these forecasted rain amounts are expected to bring rises to
small creeks and rivers in the area, there is no flooding
anticipated at this time.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to monitor the
situation and update our forecast.

rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall to the area. The first ongoing
front is expected to bring 1 to 2 inches of rain to the Juneau area
the rest of today, with the second round of heavy rain bringing an
additional 1 to 2 inches through tonight. More localized higher
amounts are possible due to terrain effects, but overall the
moderate to heavy rainfall is expected to last into the overnight
hours and Friday morning with not much of a break between the rounds
of precipitation.

forecasted amounts expected through Friday morning are expected to
bring rises to small creeks and rivers in the area. While small

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 15 at 11:40AM PDT until October 16 at 11:00AM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 10 PM THIS EVENING TO 11 AM PDT
FRIDAY DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR NORTH BAY INTERIOR
MOUNTAINS...

.Moderate offshore winds will develop Thursday evening into Friday
morning over the North Bay Interior Mountains. Conditions will be
very dry with very poor overnight humidity recoveries only reaching
14 to 24 percent. Rapid fire spread is possible given the combination
of gusty northerly winds and very dry overnight conditions.

The National Weather Service in San Francisco CA has issued a Red
Flag Warning in effect from 10 PM this evening to 11 AM PDT Friday.

* AFFECTED AREA...North Bay Interior Mountains.

* TIMING...From 10 PM this evening to 11 AM PDT Friday.

* WINDS 20 FOOT...North winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 40 mph.
The highest peaks above 4000ft will see gusts up to 60 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 16 to 20 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning is issued when weather conditions that promote
rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening are forecast.
This does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either
occurring now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple
ways to receive information from authorities.

Please advise responding agencies or fire crews in the field of this
fire weather alert.

Follow all fire restrictions. One less spark, one less wildfire.

Never leave burning debris or camp fires unattended; extinguish them
completely. Avoid using equipment or machinery that could create a
spark. Secure tow chains to avoid dragging and subsequent sparks.
Never toss cigarette butts out of your vehicle's window. Remember,
one less spark, one less flame.

Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan! Where will you go? How
will you get there? Do you have your go kit ready to go? Who will you
call to let others know you are safe? Visit ready.gov/plan for more
information.

properties.description:

Warning, which is in effect from 9 AM to 8 PM CDT Friday. A Fire
Weather Watch has also been issued. This Fire Weather Watch is in
effect from Saturday morning through Saturday evening.

* WIND...North winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph behind a
cold front.

* HUMIDITY...Minimum Relative Humidity values between 25 to 40
percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.

are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures will
create favorable weather for rapid fire growth and spread. Avoid
activities that promote open flames and sparks.

weather conditions exists. These conditions could promote the rapid
spread of wildfires which could become life-threatening. Check
www.weather.gov/jan/fireweather for forecast updates and a
possible upgrade of this watch to a Red Flag Warning.

The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has issued a
PM-10 High Pollution Advisory for Douglas on Friday.

An episode of strong and gusty winds is forecast to generate
widespread blowing dust that may result in local PM-10 concentrations
that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects increase as air
quality deteriorates.

Coarse particulate matter - also known as PM-10 - is an air
contaminant that can aggravate heart and lung disease conditions,
especially in older adults, children, and those with asthma. A
decrease in physical activity is recommended.

Consolidate your travel, stabilize loose soils, slow down or avoid
travel on dirt roads, reduce or eliminate fireplace use, and avoid
using gas-powered lawn equipment.

For details on this High Pollution Advisory,
visit the ADEQ internet site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/douglas or
call 602-771-2300.

unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

dangerous surf conditions.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued October 15 at 10:51AM CDT until October 17 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS POSSIBLE SATURDAY...

.A strong cold front will quickly move through the area Friday
afternoon. The front will be mostly if not completely dry as it
moves through the area. Quickly after it moves into the Gulf much
drier air will surge in behind it. In addition cooler air will
move in along with strong northerly winds. On Saturday sunny skies
and winds in the first 1500-3000 ft will be out of the same
direction sllowing for efficient mixing. This will help to bring
wind gusts of 15 to as high as 30 miles an hour across most
locations along and north of I-10. This will also lead to even
drier air mixing into the area helping to drop the RH into the
mid to lower 30% range with some locations seeing the relative
humidity just below 30%. This will combine with current D1 and D2
drought conditions across all of southwest Mississippi and much
of southeast LA along and northwest of a line from Thibodaux to
Franklinton. This could provide ample fuel for wildfires. The
combination of breezy to gusty winds, current drought conditions,
ample fuel, and very dry conditions will allow any fire that
develops to spread quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.

* AFFECTED AREA...Pointe Coupee, West Feliciana, East Feliciana,
St. Helena, Washington, Iberville, West Baton Rouge, East
Baton Rouge, Assumption, St. James, Wilkinson, Amite, Pike,
Northern Tangipahoa, Walthall, Southeast St. Tammany, Northern
St. Tammany, Southwestern St. Tammany, Central Tangipahoa,
Lower Tangipahoa, Northern Livingston, Southern Livingston,
Western Ascension and Eastern Ascension.

* WINDS...North 10 to 15 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 30 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
Red Flag Warnings.
